messages.subject: CODEX
parts:
Hi-

I am trying to use CODEX with the following code, but have encountered two error messages.
As you can see from the first error message, I tried to use Rsamtools to read in my bam, and
then converted the list to a dataframe. But then I ran into a second error message (bottom).
Can anyone help me troubleshoot these error messages?


CODEX - Steps
#############################################
code chunk number 3: bambedObj1
#############################################

Library(Rsamtools)
Library(CODEX)

setwd("/Data/CODEX/tumor")
dirPath_tumor <- ("/Data/CODEX/tumor")
bamFile_tumor <- list.files(dirPath_tumor, pattern='*.bam$')
bamdir_tumor <- file.path(dirPath_tumor, bamFile_tumor)

sampname <- as.matrix(read.table(file.path(dirPath_tumor, "sample.bam")))
Error in scan(file = file, what = what, sep = sep, quote = quote, dec = dec,  :
  line 1 did not have 3 elements
In addition: Warning message:
In read.table(file.path(dirPath_tumor, "sample.bam")) :
  line 1 appears to contain embedded nulls

WORK AROUND
library(Rsamtools)
bam <- scanBam("sample.bam")  // replaces the code sampname <- as.matrix(read.table(file.path(dirPath, "sampname"))) //
bam_tumor <- as.data.frame(bam)
 
sampname <- bam_tumor
bedFile_tumor <- file.path(dirPath_tumor, "sample.bed")
chr <- 1
bambedObj_tumor <- getbambed(bamdir = bamdir_tumor, bedFile=bedFile_tumor, sampname=bam_tumor, projectname="project", chr)
bamdir <- bambedObj_tumor$bamdir_tumor
sampname <- bambedObj_tumor$sampname
ref <- bambedObj_tumor$ref
projectname <- bambedObj_tumor$projectname
chr <- bambedObj_tumor$chr


#####################################
code chunk number 4:coverageObj1
#####################################

coverageObj <- getcoverage(bambedObj_tumor, mapqthres = 30) 

Getting coverage for sample K00171:238:H7JKLBBXX:6:2210:19451:33088: read length 100.
Error in BamFile(file, index) : 'file' must be character(1) and not NA


Many Thanks,
Margaret

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] CODEX
parts:
Hi Margaret,

Your bam directory doesn't correspond to a bam file. You need to specify the bam directory (that is, bamdir_tumor) correctly. bamdir_tumor is a column vector where each line is directory to a bam file in your system. Also make sure that your bam names correspond to the bam directories correctly.

Yuchao

--
Yuchao Jiang (yuc...@mail.med.upenn.edu)
PhD student in Genomics and Computational Biology
University of Pennsylvania
